instruction: Browse Barbie toys for kids and sort by lowest price.

metadata.explanation: Different toy brand (Barbie) with same category structure and sort order as original.
metadata.verification: Task uses existing check_direct_json_object metric and get_active_tab_html_parse getter. No custom functions needed. Evaluator checks breadcrumb navigation and URL parameters match expected product category and sort order.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: browsing to Barbie toys category, 'for kids' category selection, and sorting by lowest price
Getter (get_active_tab_html_parse) extracts correct state: breadcrumb navigation elements (Barbie, Toys, Kids), sort selector (Price Low-High), and URL parameters (S=4)
Metric (check_direct_json_object) performs correct comparison: checks that all expected keys (barbie, toys, kids, price low-high) are true and no unexpected filters exist (is_other_exist=false)
Data flow is semantically correct: category='class&url' mode extracts both breadcrumb elements via class_multiObject_li and URL parameters via url_include_expected_multichoice
Expected values are semantically correct: barbie/toys/kids verify category navigation, 'price low-high' verifies sort order via both breadcrumb selector text and URL parameter S=4
Evaluator provides redundancy by checking both HTML elements (breadcrumbs, sort selector) AND URL parameters, increasing robustness
